title: Auditing Diff-SAE Backdoor Isolation on Open Sleeper-Agent Models

original_idea.body:
# Auditing Diff-SAE Backdoor Isolation on Open Sleeper-Agent Models

**Problem:** Activation Differences Reveal Backdoors (arXiv:2605.07324, May 2026) shows Diff-SAE achieves a Backdoor Isolation Score of 0.40 with perfect precision on the models the authors tested, but it is unclear whether this holds for publicly released backdoored/sleeper-agent checkpoints with different trigger styles.

**Direction:** Take 2-3 open backdoored model checkpoints (e.g. published sleeper-agent or trojan-LLM weights on HuggingFace), reproduce the Diff-SAE difference-of-activations recipe at one residual-stream layer using SAELens, and measure whether the top difference-features cleanly localize the trigger. Vary trigger type (token-level vs phrase-level vs date-conditioned) and report BIS/precision per trigger type.

**Why it matters:** Unsupervised backdoor detection that needs only two model snapshots and no knowledge of the trigger is exactly the kind of monitoring infrastructure valuable outside frontier labs. Confirming or breaking the headline result on independent models tells the community whether the method generalizes.

**Relevant context:** Activation Differences Reveal Backdoors: A Comparison of SAE Architectures (arXiv:2605.07324, May 2026) reports Diff-SAE BIS 0.40, precision 1.0, FPR 0; Crosscoders BIS <0.02. Suggests backdoors are directional activation shifts, not sparse features. SAELens tooling listed in subfield context.
